register.text: For informational marketing content, treat any invitation to book a diagnostic, discuss the situation, or continue the conversation as a CTA unless the task explicitly authorises one. This includes indirect meeting prompts and direct brand-level offers such as a free 30-minute diagnostic. End with a neutral practical observation or next-step note instead of a meeting prompt.
When approved evidence presents an operational practice as policy or positioning, keep that qualifier in the copy. Do not rewrite it as an absolute guarantee or warranty-level statement.
If the source set does not support a substantive explanatory claim, replace it with a neutral workflow prompt or decision step rather than filling the gap with general background explanation.

Keep actor framing consistent with the approved persona and evidence. Do not introduce an unsupported multi-person team, staff, or broader organisational actor when the source context is an owner-operator or single business decision-maker; rewrite the example in owner-only or business-level terms instead.

Do not insert supported but off-topic company-positioning details when they do not advance the requested workflow point. If a post is meant to explain one bounded decision, control, or diagnostic, keep company facts out unless they are necessary to make that point accurately.

proposals.lesson_text: Keep actor framing consistent with the approved persona and evidence. Do not introduce an unsupported multi-person team, staff, or broader organisational actor when the source context is an owner-operator or single business decision-maker; rewrite the example in owner-only or business-level terms instead.
proposals.reason: Batch 4 adds a distinct recurring issue not yet covered in the register: unsupported expansion from owner/operator framing to a multi-person team. This is reusable persona-fit and evidence-boundary guidance, supported by the confirmed Gate finding in N117.

proposals.lesson_text: Do not insert supported but off-topic company-positioning details when they do not advance the requested workflow point. If a post is meant to explain one bounded decision, control, or diagnostic, keep company facts out unless they are necessary to make that point accurately.
proposals.reason: Batch 4 shows a new failure mode distinct from the existing lessons: even evidence-supported Bareni facts can be weak grounding if they distract from the task's required bounded workflow lesson. N121 supports a reusable scope-discipline lesson rather than a duplicate of the existing policy/guarantee lesson.
